source.title: Weil sums of binomials: properties, applications, and open problems

accepted.question_text: Let F be a finite field of characteristic 2 with even extension degree [F : F_2], let d be an invertible exponent over F, let psi be the canonical additive character of F, and define W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax) for a in F. Must there exist some a in F^* for which |W_{F,d}(a)-1| >= -1 + 2*sqrt(|F|), equivalently some a in F^* for which |W_{F,d}(a)| >= 2*sqrt(|F|)?
accepted.context_brief: Sarwate-Pursley lower bound conjecture for characteristic 2 fields of even degree

evidence.quote: Definition 1.3 (WF,d). If F is a finite field with canonical additive character ψ, and d is invertible over F, then WF,d always denotes the function from F to C with WF,d(a) = Σ_{x∈F} ψ(x^d − ax), for each a ∈ F.

Conjecture 8.11 (Sarwate-Pursley, 1980). Let F be of characteristic 2 with [F : F2] even, and let d be an invertible exponent over F. Then there is some a ∈ F∗ such that |WF,d(a)−1| ≥ −1 + 2√|F|, or equivalently, there is some a ∈ F∗ such that |WF,d(a)| ≥ 2√|F|.

accepted.question_text: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p, let l be the smallest odd prime divisor of the extension degree [F : F_p], assume [F : F_p] is not a power of 2, and let d be a nondegenerate invertible exponent over F. If V_{F,d} denotes the minimum p-adic valuation of the Weil-sum spectrum values W_{F,d}(a) for a in F^*, is it always true that V_{F,d} <= ((l+1)/(2l))*[F : F_p]?
accepted.context_brief: Conjectured sharp upper bound on p-adic valuation of Weil spectra

evidence.quote: Definition 9.1 (Valuation of Weil Spectrum VF,d). Let F be a finite field and let d be invertible over F. Then the valuation of the Weil spectrum of F and d, denoted VF,d, is VF,d = min_{a∈F∗} vp(WF,d(a)).

Conjecture 9.11 (Katz-Langevin-Lee-Sapozhnikov, 2017). If F is a finite field of characteristic p with [F : Fp] not a power of 2, if ℓ is the smallest odd prime divisor of [F : Fp], and if d is a nondegenerate invertible exponent over F, then VF,d ≤ (ℓ+1)/(2ℓ)[F : Fp].

accepted.question_text: Let F be a finite field, let d be an invertible exponent over F, and define the Weil spectrum of (F,d) to be the set {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*}, where W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax). Suppose this spectrum has exactly three distinct values. Must those three values always be symmetric, meaning that the two nonzero values are additive opposites of each other?
accepted.context_brief: Symmetry conjecture for three-valued Weil spectra

evidence.quote: Definition 1.4 (Weil Spectrum). If F is a finite field and d is an invertible exponent over F, then the Weil spectrum associated with F and d is the set {WF,d(a) : a ∈ F∗}.

We say that a three-valued WF,d is symmetric if the two nonzero values in {WF,d(a) : a ∈ F∗} are opposites of each other. It is not known whether all three-valued WF,d are symmetric, but we may conjecture it. Conjecture 10.5. If F is a finite field, d is an invertible exponent over F, and WF,d is three-valued, then it is symmetric.

accepted.question_text: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p whose extension degree [F : F_p] is a power of 2. Does there fail to exist every invertible exponent d over F for which the Weil spectrum {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*} has exactly three distinct values? Equivalently, must Helleseth's three-valued phenomenon never occur over such fields?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 10.6 (Helleseth Three-Valued Conjecture, 1971). If F is a finite field of characteristic p with [F : Fp] a power of 2, then there does not exist any invertible exponent d over F such that WF,d is three-valued.

accepted.question_text: Among all pairs (F,d) consisting of a finite field F and an invertible exponent d over F for which the Weil spectrum {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*} is three-valued, are all such pairs, up to the exponent equivalence relation generated by d ≡ p^k e mod |F^*| and d ≡ p^k e^{-1} mod |F^*|, already represented by the families listed in Table 1 of the paper?
accepted.context_brief: Completeness of the known classification of three-valued Weil sums

evidence.quote: Definition 5.7. If d and e are invertible exponents over a finite field F of characteristic p such that either d ≡ p^k e (mod |F∗|) or d ≡ p^k e^{-1} (mod |F∗|) for some integer k, then d and e are said to be equivalent exponents over F.

Of course the main open problem which encompasses all others in the realm of three-valued WF,d is whether Table 1 is in fact a complete listing of all three-valued WF,d. Open Problem 10.17. Is every pair (F, d) of finite field and invertible exponent such that WF,d is three-valued accounted for (up to the equivalence of Definition 5.7) on Table 1?

accepted.question_text: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p with |F| > 2, let d be an invertible exponent over F satisfying d ≡ 1 mod (p-1), and define W_{F,d}(a)=sum_{x in F} psi(x^d-ax) for a in F. Must there exist some nonzero a in F for which W_{F,d}(a)=0?
accepted.context_brief: Helleseth vanishing conjecture for Weil sums

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1 (Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture, 1971). If F is a finite field of characteristic p with |F| > 2, and d is an invertible exponent over F with d ≡ 1 (mod p − 1), then WF,d(a) = 0 for some a ∈ F∗.
Conjecture 11.2 (Helleseth 1971 Vanishing Conjecture, restated). If F is a finite field of characteristic p with |F| > 2, and d is an invertible exponent over F with d ≡ 1 (mod p − 1), then DF,d = 0.

Conjecture 11.4 (Helleseth’s 1971 Vanishing Conjecture, restated again). Let F be a finite field of characteristic p and order q > 2, and let d be an invertible exponent over F with d ≡ 1 (mod p − 1). Let the elements of F∗ be written b1, . . . , bq−1. Then the number of solutions (x1, . . . , xq−1) ∈ F^{q−1} to the system of equations (11) is equal to q^{q−3}.
